headline: High-risk filesystem and browser-enabled coding agent paired with offline speech model creates medium prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error exposure; no direct shared-channel evidence for criticality.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Roo Code can read/write workspace files, run browsers, and use MCP, while whisper has no tool surface to inject back. The pair still has a plausible shared-filesystem bridge via Roo Code's workspace scope, so attacker-controlled content in files or browser output could be treated as instructions by Roo Code. Whisper itself is not an injection source, so the pathway is one-way and not high.
conditions: IF Roo Code ingests workspace files or browser output as instructions without provenance checks, prompt injection is possible.
IF whisper is used only as an offline transcription model with no tool output consumed by Roo Code, this risk drops materially.
mitigations: Disable automatic instruction-following from workspace content.
Require explicit provenance labels on any text passed from whisper to Roo Code.
Keep browser-derived content in a separate review buffer.
Use a read-only handoff file for transcriptions.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance filtering between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Roo Code touches source code, browser screenshots, and model-provider API keys, and it has broad network egress; whisper touches audio and speech. If audio or transcripts are placed in the shared workspace, Roo Code can read them and may transmit context to third-party APIs. Whisper itself has no egress, so the leakage path is mediated by Roo Code rather than both agents equally.
conditions: IF audio transcripts are stored in the shared VS Code workspace, Roo Code can read them.
IF Roo Code sends workspace context to a configured model API, those transcripts may leave the local environment.
mitigations: Store transcripts outside the shared workspace.
Redact secrets before any Roo Code prompt or API call.
Restrict Roo Code to a local-only model endpoint.
Separate audio files from code workspaces.
requires-engineering: enforce per-file data-class access controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Roo Code has unrestricted workspace write, shell, git, and network capabilities, while whisper is non-runnable and has no write or network surface. The pair itself does not create symmetric conflict, but Roo Code's broad write access combined with shared filesystem state means concurrent instances can overwrite each other's workspace and git changes without locking. Uncertainty about orchestration locking pushes this to high.
conditions: IF two Roo Code instances operate on the same workspace, concurrent writes can collide.
IF git state is modified without external locking, commits or rebases can be lost or corrupted.
mitigations: Use one workspace per agent instance.
Pause one agent before the other writes.
Enable git worktrees or branch isolation.
Add a manual lock file before edits.
requires-engineering: implement workspace-level locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Roo Code can generate code, browser-derived facts, and actions, while whisper can produce transcripts that Roo Code may treat as authoritative input. Because whisper is a transformer model with no verification or action authority, the main risk is Roo Code acting on unverified transcription or browser content. That is a default interaction pathway, but not clearly irreversible.
conditions: IF Roo Code uses whisper transcripts as source-of-truth without verification, downstream mistakes can cascade.
IF Roo Code executes shell or git actions based on those transcripts, errors can propagate into code or repository state.
mitigations: Require human review before shell or git actions.
Cross-check transcripts against the original audio.
Mark whisper output as untrusted input.
Limit Roo Code to read-only analysis for first pass.
requires-engineering: add verification gates before any action-taking tool use.

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, residency, or certification mismatch is documented for this pair. Roo Code handles source code and browser screenshots, while whisper handles audio and speech; the only clear compliance issue is that Roo Code may send data to configured model APIs, but whisper has no network egress. Because the relevant compliance surfaces are not both present, the risk is limited and mostly configuration-dependent.
conditions: IF regulated audio or transcripts are routed into Roo Code's configured third-party model API, compliance obligations may apply.
IF the deployment requires data residency controls that the configured API does not meet, a mismatch exists.
mitigations: Keep regulated audio out of Roo Code prompts.
Use a residency-approved model endpoint.
Disable retention on any external API used by Roo Code.
Document data-class handling for transcripts.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and retention.
